This comparison analyzes the demographic and diagnostic characteristics of pediatric and adult patients receiving [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (BMSL), based on data from the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]]. The data highlights significant differences in disease prevalence, age distributions, and gender splits between the two cohorts.

In terms of diagnoses, [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]] is the clear leader for both groups, accounting for 299 children (69%) and 7,573 adults (60%) [^src1]. [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] follows as the second most common condition, affecting 136 children (31%) and 4,995 adults (39%) [^src1]. Notably, [[dk830f-primaer-skleroserende-kolangitis|DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]] and [[dk912b-korttarmssyndrom|DK912B Korttarmssyndrom]] act as outliers in this comparison; they are exclusively represented in the pediatric cohort with 59 and 24 patients, respectively, while recording zero cases among adults [^src1].

The gender distribution reveals a slight male predominance in children, with 237 boys (54%) compared to 198 girls (46%) [^src1]. In contrast, the adult cohort is perfectly balanced, with women and men each representing exactly 50% of the population (6,381 and 6,270 patients, respectively) [^src1]. Regarding age, the pediatric group has a mean age of 14 (range 4;18) and a median of 15 [^src1]. The adult group is significantly older, with a mean age of 44 (range 17;98) and a median of 42 [^src1]. Because this data represents a single snapshot in time, no longitudinal trends can be established.

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner aldersfordeling, køn og diagnosefordeling blandt børn og voksne i BMSL-behandling, og viser at DK50 og DK51 dominerer, mens DK830F og DK912B kun findes blandt børn.
